subject.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)

question: Should OpenClaw treat standalone `antml:`/`mm:` invoke blocks and `<function_calls>`-wrapped invoke blocks as leaked tool-call data in both visible replies and persisted assistant history, while preserving bare invoke XML as user content?
rationale: The patch is technically narrow and tested, but the persistence path irreversibly changes what durable transcript data is retained; tests cannot determine that product policy.

options.title: Adopt the qualified-leak boundary
options.body: Merge the current narrow allow-list because the observed proxy degradation carries a namespace or wrapper signature and bare examples remain intact.

options.title: Limit removal to delivery
options.body: Strip qualified markup only from user-visible replies and retain raw persisted text if transcript fidelity is more important than cross-path symmetry.

options.title: Pause for provider-owned recovery
options.body: Defer this sanitizer policy if maintainers want degraded invoke text classified or recovered through provider metadata instead of removed.

recommendation.title: Adopt the qualified-leak boundary
recommendation.body: Merge the current narrow allow-list because the observed proxy degradation carries a namespace or wrapper signature and bare examples remain intact.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans shared visible-text behavior and durable session history rather than the contributor's isolated repair implementation.
